title: Relative Formula Mass and Moles

figures_added.what: Coin-bag figure (currentColor, fill-opacity) for the count-atoms-by-weighing hook

opener_concept: Counting hidden coins in a sealed bag by weight (120 g / 3 g = 40), then naming it as moles = mass ÷ Mr (Mr is the weight of one 'unit').
notes: Bank was arithmetically clean on fresh-solve: all 14 problems verified (Mr additions, moles = mass/Mr both ways, % by mass, conservation of mass). No numbers changed.

Added full guided infrastructure: guided.opener, guided.teach.{bronze,silver,gold} (MgCl2 Mr / %H in water / (NH4)2SO4 Mr, all off-bank), tier_guides, {tier}_description, per-problem hint, and guided_steps with phase:substitute boundaries on every problem.

Every misconception given a derived 'expect' (committed the error): forgot_subscript H2O->17, CO2->28, H2SO4->49, %O CO2->36.4, urea N->23.3; inverse_error 44/44->1936(x), 0.5molH2O->36, 8g Mg->3, CaCO3->400, 2.5molNaOH->16, 2.4g Mg->10; Ca(OH)2 forgot_bracket->58, forgot_subscript->57; conservation wrong_equation->6.4. Non-determinate errors (NaOH wrong_Mr, urea wrong_count) set expect:null.
No unit-conversion boxes needed: every mass is already in grams and Mr in g/mol (base units for moles = mass/Mr). Noted per science-delta rule.
Board-neutral: no board named, no equation-sheet claim; chemistry equations are recall for all boards anyway.
